{{Short description|American physicist (1927–2012)}}
'''George Fred Koster''' (1927–2012) was an American physicist.

== Biography ==
Foster served in the [[United States Navy]] during [[World War II]].<ref name="bglegacy">{{cite news |title=George F. Koster |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/bostonglobe/name/george-koster-obituary?id=20881081 |access-date=20 July 2023 |work=Boston Globe |date=14–21 May 2012}}</ref> He completed his doctoral dissertation in 1951, titled ''The Effects of Configuration Interaction on the Hyperfine Structure'', advised by [[Bernard Taub Feld]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]],<ref>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref> and later joined the MIT faculty. While teaching at MIT, Foster was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1962.<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=K&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=20 July 2023 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>

Foster was married to Frances J. Grigg until her death in 2010.<ref name="bglegacywife">{{cite news |title=Frances J. Koster |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/bostonglobe/name/frances-koster-obituary?id=23450113 |access-date=20 July 2023 |work=Boston Globe |date=19–20 March 2010}}</ref> The couple raised three children.<ref name="bglegacy"/><ref name="bglegacywife"/> Foster died in [[Brookline, Massachusetts]], in May 2012, aged 85.<ref name="bglegacy"/><ref name="mitobit">{{cite news |title=George Koster, physics professor emeritus, dies at 85 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2012/obit-koster |access-date=20 July 2023 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=21 May 2012}}</ref>
